Shameful & Disturbing Incident Outside Mani’s, Mulund (18th Oct 2025)
This review isn’t about food — it’s about basic humanity, which I saw completely missing outside Mani’s, Mulund West on the evening of 18th October 2025 (Saturday) during Diwali time.
While I was having dosa with my family, I witnessed something horrifying — a tall man in a kurta slapped and dragged a young beggar girl right outside the café. She must have been barely 10–12 years old. He hit her so hard, then grabbed her by her t-shirt and pulled her, while everyone just stood there and watched. It was one of the most disgusting things I’ve ever seen.
And what shocked me most — not one single person from Mani’s staff or management came forward. No one tried to stop that man or even check on that child. Everyone simply ignored it as if nothing happened. Even after assaulting her, that man came back to collect his parcel calmly while his wife sat in the car watching!
I want to ask Mani’s management — do your CCTV cameras not work? Did no staff member see this? Why didn’t anyone step up? It happened right at your doorstep. If you claim to be a family-friendly place, you also have a moral responsibility to protect people outside your premises, especially a child being assaulted in public view.
That moment made me lose all respect for this place. Good food means nothing when basic humanity and courage are missing. I truly hope Mani’s management takes this seriously, checks their CCTV footage from 18th October, identifies that man, and at least reports this inhuman act. Silence in such situations is shameful.

What made the experience even better was the courteous and attentive staff, who ensured we were comfortable and served promptly despite the busy crowd. The ambience is simple but clean and welcoming, suitable for both quick meals and family outings.

Overall, Thambbi offers a truly satisfying South Indian dining experience that delivers on taste, authenticity, and hospitality. Highly recommended for anyone craving comforting, vegetarian South Indian food in the heart of Mulund.

featured_reviews.review_text:

The Uttappa was equally impressive, fluffy and generously topped, with just the right balance of spices. Their Filter Coffee was rich, aromatic, and beautifully brewed — a true South Indian classic.

Vishwa Bharati Veg Restaurant, standing as a symbol of culinary legacy for over 50 years, remains an emblem of timeless taste and unwavering quality. The Dal Rice, a simple yet flavorful dish, and the Puri Bhaji, despite a slight saltiness in the bhaji, showcased the restaurant's commitment to maintaining traditional flavors.

The journey of flavors continued with the Dahi Vada, a dish that melted hearts with its exquisite softness and mouthwatering taste, triggering a nostalgic rush reminiscent of cherished childhood memories.

The staff, with their attentive and polite service, added to the overall pleasant experience. Vishwa Bharati Veg Restaurant not only offers delicious food but also carries the warmth of nostalgia, making every visit a reminiscent journey back in time. Rooted in homestyle cooking and honest flavours, we serve comforting South Indian meals that remind you of home. Whether it’s breakfast, a quick bite or filter coffee conversations, Mangalore Tiffin Room is your neighbourhood spot for true Mangalorean taste.

We got the Ghee podi Masala Dosa.I've definitely had crispier dosa, but the potato masala was on point and the quantity of the masala was also good.

The mangalore buns felt undercooked and doughy from the inside. We pointed this out to the cashier, who, after a lot of back and forth asked the chef to prepare fresh ones for us. We did want the replacement but they were kind enough to insist and give it to us in a takeaway box.

The best thing we had here was the filter coffee soft serve. The coffee taste and the sweetness were balanced perfectly as per our liking.

featured_reviews.name: Sanchit Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located in Nahur, this South Indian breakfast place is one of the new outlets riding a wave of popularising idli and dosas in the city!

The place is pretty small and people have to have their food while standing. Good thing is their kitchen is visible so we know what goes behind the scenes!

The staff is pretty quick with the orders and friendly, the turn around time is actually good since it's a small outlet while in the kitchen it's very well organized like a smooth oiled machine.

Coming over to the food, I have tried
1) Mangalore Buns: This is a rarity in Mumbai and glad they have kept it. The buns are freshly made and they are crisp from outside and soft from inside. They just have to make sure its fried at the right temperature as at times the outer layer gets blacked out.

2) Benne dosa: Crisp form outside and soft from inside but they lack the thickness which is required. The amount of ghee added feels a bit more but unlike one popular chain known for it! They can try making it more thicker.

3) Goli Bhajji: Another of my favorites, crisp golden on outside but they left it a bit chewy inside. Would be better to add a bit of dry coconut piece to enhance the taste.

4) Thatte idli: Idli is actually good here with it being soft and smooth

5) Masala Podi dosa: The masala dosa was pretty different from what you usually get in Mumbai. It's not the paper dosa but also not like the Benne dosa. Overall it was amazing and the potato palya was tasty!

6) Filter Coffee: The filter coffee tastes good here whereas I also tried the cold filter coffee but it wasn't that fun!

7) Coconut chutney and Sambhar: Coconut chutney is good over here and freshly made, same for sambhar but unfortunately I didn't find the consistency across my 3 visits for the sambar. During the first two visits the sambhar was actually tasty and the recent visit, it turned watery and more spicy... More like the Tamil Nadu style over Karnataka style!

Overall it's a good place for breakfast and no need to head all the way to Bandra or fancy places to try out expensive dosas as here they serve for an affordable price.

featured_reviews.name: Niv Shetye
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mangalore Tiffin Room – A Hidden South Indian Gem in Mulund 📍

Discovered through the ever-reliable Instagram algorithm, Mangalore Tiffin Room turned out to be one suggestion that truly lived up to the hype. For lovers of authentic South Indian flavors, this small outlet is definitely a hidden gem worth exploring.

Ambience & Setup

Don’t expect a traditional dine-in experience here. The outlet has no formal seating, but they provide a few side tables where you can comfortably enjoy your food while standing. It’s a small, fast-food style joint with a minimalistic look, capable of accommodating around 15–20 people at a time. Simple setup, but the focus here is clearly on the food.

What We Tried

Benne Masala Dosa
Simple yet packed with flavor. The dosa had a nice buttery aroma and delivered a satisfying, classic South Indian taste.

Vada Sambar Dip
A straightforward dish with two average-sized Medu Vadas served in sambar. It was decent, though nothing extraordinary.

Ghee Podi Thatte Idli
This one was a pleasant surprise! Soft, fluffy thatte idlis coated with ghee and podi masala created a beautiful balance of simplicity and flavor.

Bun Parotta with Kurma
Two perfectly cooked Kerala-style Bun Parottas that were flaky and flavorful. While the parotta itself was excellent, the kurma gravy felt a bit underwhelming.

Filter Kaapi Ice Cream ⭐
The unexpected star of the visit. Unique, refreshing, and bursting with coffee flavor—definitely something you shouldn’t miss.

Overall Verdict

Almost everything on the menu is priced under ₹140, making it fairly pocket-friendly. While a few dishes could improve, the overall experience is satisfying—especially for those craving authentic South Indian comfort food.

If you’re around Mulund, Mangalore Tiffin Room is a great spot to explore for simple, flavorful, and affordable South Indian bites.

I recently visited this dosa snack corner tucked in near mulund railway station (West) opposite to Bhaucha vadapav. The place may be petite, but its flavorful dosas that leaves a lasting impression.

The menu offers a variety of dosas to cater to different tastes. From the classic masala dosa to the Chinese masala dosa Or mysore masala dosa, there's something for everyone. The dosas are reasonably priced, making it an affordable treat for a quick snack.

The ambiance is okayish, with a few tables and chairs arranged neatly. It's a perfect place for a quick bite.

The dosas are made to order, ensuring a crisp texture and authentic south indian taste. The chutneys served alongside are a flavorful complement.

The service is friendly and prompt. Despite the small space, the staff manages to create a welcoming atmosphere. It's a great spot for a solo snacks.

if you're in the mood for a tasty dosa without breaking the bank, this small dosa corner is worth a visit with a satisfying experience.

featured_reviews.name: May D'velra
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is located opposite to the famous Bhau vadapav near mulund west station. The location is prime and is quite visible from roadside. Please don't go buy the ambience. It's a place of 9 tables inside the restaurant. They serve different varieties and types of dosas and uttapad and pav bhaji. They have almost 100 types of dosa varieties. This place is a hidden gem. The dosa is simply delicious and mouth watering. The service is just great. Please try Chinese masala dosa and you will keep on having it. Also they serve the best pav bhaji and to tell you guys the quantity is so justified with the quality is worth every penny. Along with the pav bhaji they serve the cucumber which adds the best taste to it. Uttapa are simply mouth watering you order any and I bet you won't be disappointed. Dosa are their gem and I would say the best at making. They also serve soft drinks. This place is affordable and in budget. Do visit this place with your friends family and loved ones otherwise you yourself can hog on the food anytime.
